entity.name: EoS Foundation
entity.description: EoS Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit building a free, open-source embedded operating system framework in pure C11. The project includes an RTOS kernel (15.8 KB flash, 26.0 KB RAM on Cortex-M4), a secure two-stage bootloader (eBoot), a build system supporting 171 MCUs (eBuild), a multi-platform simulator (EoSim, 153 platforms), and open hardware designs (eCAD, 125 product lines). All software is MIT-licensed across 23 repositories with approximately 500,000 lines of code and 14 free educational books.

projects.name: EoS RTOS Kernel
projects.description: A real-time operating system kernel written in pure C11, designed for deeply embedded systems. Features preemptive multitasking, priority-based scheduling, inter-task communication, and a minimal footprint of 15.8 KB flash and 26.0 KB RAM on ARM Cortex-M4.

projects.name: eBoot Secure Bootloader
projects.description: A secure two-stage bootloader for embedded systems with hardware-backed cryptographic verification, supporting AES and SHA-256/512.

projects.name: eBuild Build System
projects.description: A build system supporting 171 microcontrollers across multiple architectures, enabling cross-platform embedded development with a single unified toolchain.

projects.name: EoSim Simulator
projects.description: A multi-platform simulator supporting 153 embedded platforms, enabling development and testing without physical hardware.

projects.name: eCAD Open Hardware Designs
projects.description: Open-source hardware designs covering 125 product lines, 15 development boards, and 4 health monitoring devices. All designs are freely available for modification and manufacture.

plans.name: Infrastructure and Development Support
plans.description: Sustain ongoing development of the EoS embedded OS framework, including CI/CD infrastructure, testing across 171 MCU targets, documentation, and community support.

plans.name: Monthly Sustainer
plans.description: Recurring monthly support to fund ongoing maintenance, security updates, and new MCU platform support.
